definitions: To begin and seem likely to continue for a period of time, especially of something unwelcome or unpleasant.
To become established or entrenched, often referring to a condition or feeling.
examples: The cold weather is setting in.
A feeling of despair was setting in.
The rot is setting in on the old fence.
pastTenses: set in (past simple), set in (present perfect), set in (past perfect)
